questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: b = a makes a second name for the SAME list. Appending through b changes the one list that a also points to.

questions.question: In Python, what is a variable, really?
options: A box that contains a copy of the value
A name that points to a value in memory
questions.explanation: Python variables are labels (names) attached to objects in memory. Several names can point to the same object.

questions.question: How do you get a separate copy of a list called `a`?
questions.explanation: a.copy() creates a new list with the same items. Changing b then won't affect a.

questions.question: What does Python's garbage collection do?
options: Frees memory used by values that no name points to anymore
Empties the Trash on your Mac
questions.explanation: When nothing refers to a value anymore, Python reclaims its memory automatically, so you don't have to.
